Adding my 2c (not that anyone's asked for it): there is no change in semantics here, strictly speaking. The order of aggregation results was arbitrary and now it's deterministic (which one could argue is a certain kind of arbitrary).

Problem is that fundamentally it makes no sense for `x - x` to produce any other result than zero (across `x`'s label set). But with `x` an aggregation of aggregations (a quite common case, e.g. a sum of an average by `instance`) and without a deterministic ordering of aggregation results, this is not actually true in PromQL. In the same way that it makes no sense for valid (monotonically increasing) histogram buckets to become invalid after 2 rounds of aggregation.

> Adding my 2c (not that anyone's asked for it)

I value your opinion. Thanks for your input.

Forgive me if I misunderstood: “`sum by` returns results sorted by labels” seems a definite change in semantics to me. 

Even if you document this cannot be relied on, people will rely on it.

I am wondering how the PromQL compliance would look like if data comes in different order in different softwares while using the same PromQL package and having the same raw series/samples. Would that become non compliant because of floating point error while technically being compliant?

We could try running the PromQL compliance test on Prometheus with this change and see if it still passes as a quick and easy check (just to see if things break, but does not assure that it wont break other softwares if Prometheus passes).

BTW this is where they are sorted, right before the code changed in this PR gets called: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/e261eccb35ee5ce4f024ab079c848e39660066ed/promql/engine.go#L1167-L1169

I can see the change in semantics argument, even if in my personal view a weak one. And it may make sense to document it as such, even though the TSDB also "happens to" return time series sorted by their labels and I doubt that's explicitly documented anywhere. And particularly, I doubt there's anywhere in API or user documentation where it says "raw time series returned by the TSDB are sorted, but aggregation results are not". (If there were such a statement anywhere, that would make it a much stronger argument.)

As for this change actually breaking anything, I don't see how that would be possible. Existing Prometheus versions return aggregation results in randomized order; this would return them in a fixed order. If anything would get broken by the fixed result order, it would also be broken whenever the randomization happened to produce the same ordering. I.e. it would be an existing issue, not something introduced by this change. And would have to be fixed regardless.
I do not think the PromQL conformance tests run aggregations on top of aggregations, and this is where results could change.

What I am worried about is that we can never make a future change that changes the order without breaking people that have come to rely on it. For comparison, Go maps intentionally randomise the order so people can't rely on it.

It might be consider a problem with pie chart or a very minor issue, but IMHO it shows that based on approach taken by Prometheus here there might be consequence for downstream consumers of metrics - they might need to compensate for undefined order depending on use case. Having output more stable would make this whole class of issues (and extra code in all consumers) go away.

Since this technically changes the query results for the same raw data + query for some pattern of queries, and since this bring in ordering for the grouping in aggregation, I would prefer if we document it and add this case also in the compliance test suite while following the protocol for bringing in any changes in the compliance.

> TSDB also "happens to" return time series sorted by their labels

In PromQL engine, we use `querier.Select(false, hints, n.LabelMatchers...)`, where the `false` means the TSDB is not required to return sorted series and give in any order. Being sorted might just be a side effect of how storage is structured, but it not a requirement.

We are not bringing any ordering or sorting - we just ensure the stability of aggregations for the same set of inputs. That is a difference to me. It is unclear if/where this should be documented and I do not think we should have this as a requirement to be compliant? cc @juliusv

If the fact that TSDB results "happen to be sorted" does not need to be documented, then neither does this. Or conversely, if this needs to be documented, then so does the fact that TSDB accidentally returns sorted results. (o:

As for aggregations sorting labels (not label values) lexicographically (which Bryan pointed to above), that is something that Prometheus already does now, not something introduced by this change. No idea whether that's documented anywhere, so possibly something else that should be explicitly documented, if you decide to go down that path.

I will be on PTO for more than a week now. So to not keep this hanging on me: I am not against this PR and I actually don't have a strong opinion on this for compliance, so I would go ahead with what you all decide is the best :), while my take is the stability should not be just in Prometheus but also mandated in compliant solutions (but that should not block this PR).

> We are sorting the labels, not the metrics, if I am correct.

Thank you @roidelapluie, you are correct and I was completely mistaken. Apologies.

Moreover, Prometheus sorts results alphabetically by labels as the last step of every [EDIT: range] query:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/fdbc40a9efcc8197a94f23f0e479b0b56e52d424/promql/engine.go#L658

So I still think this behaviour should be documented, but the change I was worried about happened more than 5 years ago.
I no longer have any concerns or objections about this PR.

it happens that we sort the select because we use mergequerier (we query heads+blocks, so it must be sorted to merge correctly)

We never use this shortcut:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/fdbc40a9efcc8197a94f23f0e479b0b56e52d424/storage/merge.go#L104

because we have 2 queriers all the time, which means we always want series sorted from TSDB:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/fdbc40a9efcc8197a94f23f0e479b0b56e52d424/tsdb/db.go#L1575


So, while PromQL uses Select(false), it is true in a Prometheus setup.

I'd just merge this PR as is, it seems generally good for our users to have reproducible results.

issue_context.title: PromQL is not deterministic
issue_context.body:
Was trying to debug why a Grafana Heatmap panel for a histogram that clearly only had recorded observations in the 1M-2M and 2M-5M ranges looked like this:

![Screenshot from 2021-10-05 12-53-51](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32070098/136010304-9e6ee95b-b8f8-45bd-a09e-fddf7c1103df.png)

You'll notice that the 2 buckets above had on the order of 30K observations each, whereas the other non-zero ones all show up as `0.0` (rounded). I also noticed that on refresh the `0.0` buckets shift around randomly. The underlying query is nothing fancy:

```
sum by (le) (
  avg by(le, some_label) (
    increase(metric[1m])
  )
)
```

Long story short, I looked at a specific timestamp and played around with the query and what seems to happen is that aggregations (such as `sum` and `avg`) produce randomly ordered results. If those results are in turn aggregated again, the result of that aggregation may be different depending on the order of the inputs.

Take for example the following query:

```
sum(
  avg by(foo) (
      label_replace(up{job="prometheus"}, "foo", "1", "job", "prometheus") * 0.99999999999998
    or
      label_replace(up{job="prometheus"}, "foo", "2", "job", "prometheus") * 100
    or
      label_replace(up{job="prometheus"}, "foo", "3", "job", "prometheus") * 100
  )
)
```

On any single-Prometheus deployment, this will sometimes yield `200.99999999999997`, sometimes `201`. The reason for that can be seen in [this playground example](https://play.golang.org/p/yZAGWt5OfiQ): `0.99999999999998 + 100.0 + 100.0 != 100.0 + 100.0 + 0.99999999999998`.

AFAICT the fix is to simply sort the output of `evaluator.aggregation()` by labels. Then in the example above `avg` will always produce the same output at a given timestamp. Not only that, but in the case of aggregating histogram buckets, the labels other than `le` will be sorted consistently across buckets, so the result of the aggregation will be exactly the same for buckets that have the same number of observations.
comments: As a side-note, while adding a bit of overhead to aggregations, this would fix the annoyance of Prometheus sometimes producing nicely sorted, sometimes randomly shuffled results.

Alternately, in order to avoid unnecessary overhead, one could simply sort the inputs to aggregations instead. If already sorted (such as when read from the TSDB) that would take linear time. If not, O(N * log(N)).

review_comments: Nice. This is actually a lot less overhead than explicitly sorting the results.
